newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL TO AUCTION OFF 2ND STATE BANK THURSDAY.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL TO AUCTION OFF 2ND STATE BANK THURSDAY.

text.p: Brazil is due to privatize its second state-owned bank Thursday when a controlling stake in Minas Gerais state's bank Credireal goes on sale at an auction for at least 121.3 million reais.

Minas Gerais will auction 986.6 million shares or 89.9 percent of Credireal's total capital at the auction, as a 10 percent stake reserved to staff was fully acquired by the bank employees, retirees and pension fund.

The Credireal sale follows the privatization of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj, which was bought by Brazil's second largest private bank Banco Itau in June. Eight financial institutions have prequalified for the Credireal selloff, but at least one bidder -- General Electric Co's General Electric Capital Corp -- has already dropped out.

The other investors are Credit Commerciale de France's CCF do Brasil; BankBoston Corp's Brazil unit; Banco Industrial e Comercial (Bicbanco); Banco Noroeste ; Companhia de Investimentos Latinoamericana; Tabal Participacoes, and Varejo SA Administracao e Participacao.
Cia de Investimentos Latinoamericana is a company created by Brazi's Banco Pactual to seek opportunities in the country's banking sector for investors.
Tabal Participacoes and Varejo are units of local Bozano Simonsen group, which owns investment bank Banco Bozano, Simonsen.
Most investors are silent on whether they will place bids, but Gazeta Mercantil newspaper reported today that Bicbanco is one of the strongest candidates for the purchase of Credireal.
The paper said Bicbanco would be highly interested in acquiring the bank as part of a growth strategy.
Bicbanco, it added, is a medium-sized bank with 3.6 billion reais in total assets.
No officials at the bank were immediately available for comment on the report.

The full list of investors who will actually participate in the auction will be only provided early Thursday before the auction takes place at 1630 local/1930 GMT on the Minas Gerais-Espirito Santo-Brasilia Stock Exchange (BOVMESB), a bolsa official said.
Prequalified investors interested in bidding for Credireal still have to present financial guarantees by late Wednesday, she added.
Credireal, formally known as Banco de Credito Real de Minas Gerais SA, has 86 branches, of which 42 are in the southeastern state of Minas Gerais.
The bank's net worth is estimated at 98 million reais.
